title: Sales enablement: Prospect playbook — positioning, messaging, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:
This playbook is a single-source sales enablement reference for prospect-facing motions: positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs, pitch deck outlines, pricing guidance for discovery conversations, customer case study summaries, and a prospect-friendly security FAQ. Use this page during discovery, technical evaluation, and executive follow-ups.

Target audience:
- AE/SDR/SDR managers running demo and discovery calls
- Solutions engineers and technical sellers supporting PoCs
- Sales leadership preparing deal strategy and pricing approvals

Owner & maintenance:
- Owner: Aisha Patel (Go-to-market)
- Review cadence: quarterly or when product/pricing changes materially
- Contributors: Product marketing, Solutions Engineering, Security & Compliance

1) Positioning & core messaging (30s/2min/5min variants)
- 30-second elevator (for execs):
  - "Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes running LLMs predictable, fast, and cost-efficient across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We help engineering teams reduce latency and unit cost while keeping deployment flexibility and enterprise controls for production workloads."
- 2-minute technical summary (for platform/infra buyers):
  - Key capabilities: high-throughput GPU-optimized runtime, automatic batching & KV caching, model catalog + quantization profiles, and smart routing for cost/latency tradeoffs.
  - Deployment modes: Hosted API (fastest time-to-value), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + SLA), Private (VPC/on-prem with KMS integration).
  - Differentiators: Production-first tooling (rollouts, tracing, cost/latency breakdowns), unified experience across environments, built-in fallback/routing policies to preserve availability.
- 5-minute product demo script (for technical evals):
  1. Quick overview: product modes + model catalog (60s)
  2. Live demo: Redwood API text generation + streaming + function calling (120s)
  3. Ops/observability: Console dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, tracing (60s)
  4. Enterprise controls: VPC/private deployment, KMS, audit logs (60s)

2) Competitive brief (one-page cheat sheet)
- Competitors to call out: Cloud-managed endpoints (large cloud providers), LLM API providers, self-hosted inference vendors.
- Primary battlecards:
  - Cloud-managed endpoints: Strengths — integrated infra, enterprise contracts; Weaknesses — unpredictable per-token economics at scale, limited model catalog tuning for inference economics.
  - LLM API providers: Strengths — simple API, broad model access; Weaknesses — limited private deployment options, less control over latency/cost tradeoffs.
  - Inference runtime vendors (self-hosted): Strengths — complete control; Weaknesses — heavy ops burden, longer time-to-value, missing unified hosted experience.
- Winning themes (talk tracks):
  1. Cost predictability at scale: show examples of batching + KV caching and estimated unit-cost improvements versus naive hosting.
  2. Production reliability: fallback policies, multi-region routing, and SLA-backed Dedicated plans.
  3. Operational visibility: token-level cost/latency, rollout tools, and alerting tied to prompt sets/evals.
  4. Enterprise controls: Private deployments + KMS + audit logging for regulated industries.

3) Pitch deck recommended slide flow (10–12 slides)
- Slide 1 — Title & TL;DR: one-line value prop tailored to prospect (e.g., "Reduce LLM inference costs by 40% while meeting latency SLAs").
- Slide 2 — Team & credibility: brief company background, Series C, engineering-first focus.
- Slide 3 — Problem statement: model fragility, unpredictable latency, and rising token costs at scale. Use prospect-specific metrics if available.
- Slide 4 — Redwood solution: unified inference platform (hosted, dedicated, private) with key bullets.
- Slide 5 — How it works (high level): serving runtime, smart routing, caching, and model catalog. Use simple diagram (1–2 lines describing components).
- Slide 6 — Performance & cost benchmarks: sample throughput and p50/p95 latency numbers for common models and expected cost per 1M tokens under typical configs.
- Slide 7 — Security & compliance: SOC2, encryption, private deployment options, logging — link to security FAQ appendix.
- Slide 8 — Pricing and commercial model: short summary, see Pricing Guidance section.
- Slide 9 — Case studies: 2 short examples with outcomes (latency/cost/SLO improvements).
- Slide 10 — Delivery & timeline: recommended pilot (2–6 weeks), key milestones, success criteria.
- Slide 11 — TCO & ROI: brief worked example comparing current infra vs Redwood (batching + dedicated).
- Slide 12 — Next steps & ask: technical deep-dive, PoC kickoff, contract owner.

Slide assets & appendix:
- Include consoles screenshots (token breakdown, route dashboards), sample API calls, and short runbook excerpt for Dedicated onboarding. Keep one-slide appendix for security/compliance details.

4) Pricing guidance (discovery & negotiation playbook)
- Pricing models overview:
  - Hosted API: pay-as-you-go (per-token / per-embedding) with free trial credits.
  - Dedicated: monthly/annual reserved capacity with throughput commitments and overage options.
  - Private: platform fee + optional support and deployment services.
- Discovery checklist (to pick initial price path):
  1. Expected token volume (monthly) and peak concurrency
  2. Latency SLOs (p50/p95 targets) and burst/throughput requirements
  3. Data residency / compliance constraints
  4. Preferred deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Rules of thumb for commercial conversations:
  - <$50k ARR prospects: emphasize Hosted + rapid time-to-value, reference docs and self-serve.
  - $50k–$250k ARR: recommend Dedicated pilot with 3-month commit; propose a blended rate that models batching gains.
  - >$250k ARR / enterprise: propose Private or Dedicated with annual commit, include SLA, onboarding, and premium support add-ons.
- Negotiation levers: commitment term, committed throughput, SLA targets, support level, and feature/metric-based ramp credits.

5) Case studies (two short vignettes for sales use)
- Case study 1 — Fintech Analytics Platform (Mid-market)
  - Problem: Real-time document summarization at 100 qps with p95 latency target <350ms; high per-token costs on baseline setup.
  - Solution: Dedicated GPU pool + aggressive KV prefix caching + quantized model variant for inference.
  - Outcome: 42% reduction in per-token cost, p95 latency from 620ms -> 280ms, successful rollout to production in 6 weeks.
- Case study 2 — Customer Support SaaS (AI-native startup)
  - Problem: Chatbot quality regressions during model upgrades and lack of rollout tooling.
  - Solution: Use Redwood rollouts + canary configurations and built-in evals for prompt sets; fallback routing to cheaper variant during high load.
  - Outcome: Zero customer-facing regressions during two major model upgrades; 18% unit-cost reduction through smarter routing over 3 months.

6) Security FAQ (prospect-focused; short answers)
- Q: Do you have SOC 2 / ISO / third-party attestations?
  - A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001. We surface audit reports to enterprise customers via our compliance portal.
- Q: How is data protected in transit and at rest?
  - A: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 encryption at rest. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Q: Can we run Redwood in our VPC or on-prem?
  - A: Yes — Private deployment mode supports VPC and an on-prem appliance option. We provide a validated deployment reference and professional services for initial rollout.
- Q: Where is customer data stored (data residency)?
  - A: Hosted data residency follows region selection (us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast-1). Dedicated can be provisioned in specific cloud regions; Private keeps data under customer control per deployment.
- Q: Do you log requests and outputs? What retention?
  - A: Platform logs request metadata and optional payloads. Default storage retention is 90 days for hosted; enterprise customers can request extended retention or custom retention policies for Dedicated/Private. Logging of model outputs is opt-in and controlled via account settings.
- Q: How do you handle encryption keys?
  - A: Hosted: Redwood-managed keys by default; Private: customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. We support BYOK for Private and Dedicated where required.
- Q: What access controls and RBAC exist?
  - A: Console-level RBAC with role templates (admin, developer, auditor). API tokens support scoped permissions and short-lived credentials. Audit logs capture changes to roles and deployments.
- Q: How do you support compliance audits?
  - A: We provide compliance packages (SOC 2 evidence bundle, network diagrams, control narratives) and a named security liaison for enterprise prospects during audits.

7) Technical evaluation / PoC checklist (2–6 week pilot)
- Phase 0 — Kickoff (week 0): NDA, security questionnaire, scope & success criteria.
- Phase 1 — Integration & baseline (week 1–2): onboard model, run baseline throughput and latency tests (p50/p95), collect token usage.
- Phase 2 — Optimization (week 2–4): enable batching/cache/quant profiles, test rollouts & fallback routing.
- Phase 3 — Evaluation & handoff (week 4–6): performance dashboard review, cost model comparison, SRE handoff for Dedicated/Private onboarding.
- Success criteria examples: p95 < target latency, unit-cost < X% above projected committed price, no reliability regressions for 48h under production-like load.

8) Objection handling (common prospects concerns)
- "We can host ourselves": Acknowledge control benefits and quantify ops cost + time-to-market of building equivalent routing, rollout, and observability features. Offer a joint TCO model.
- "Vendor lock-in": Emphasize model/version pinning, exportable configs, and on-prem/private deployment options.
- "Security compliance": Offer SOC 2 evidence, Named security contact, and Private deployment options.

9) Assets & templates (links)
- Pitch deck template: /assets/sales/pitch-deck-redwood-template.pptx
- Pricing playbook spreadsheet: /assets/sales/pricing-playbook.xlsx
- PoC runbook: /assets/tech/poc-runbook.md
- Security appendix: /assets/security/soc2-evidence-summary.pdf

10) Next steps & owner actions
- For AEs: customize slide 1 with prospect metrics and send the Security FAQ appendix at RFP stage.
- For SEs: schedule a 60–90 minute architecture workshop during PoC kickoff and capture baseline telemetry for cost modeling.
- For Sales Leadership: review pricing term deviations >15% with Pricing Committee.

Appendix A — Example discovery questions (short list)
- What are your current p95 latency targets and monthly token volumes?
- Are there regulatory or data residency requirements?
- Do you need customer-managed keys or audit evidence?
- Which model families are you evaluating (open weights vs hosted models)?

Appendix B — One-page example TCO (text)
- Baseline: self-hosted on general-purpose VMs, 1.2M tokens/day, average throughput 50 qps, p95=600ms.
- Redwood Dedicated: quantized model + batching -> expected token cost drop ~35–45%; 3-month pilot shows breakeven on infra+ops in 9 months.
